Theorem
[Uniqueness for wave equation] 1. ch2:2.4-thm-5\group Energy Methods There is at most one $u\in C^2(\overline U_T)$ satisfying (45).
Proof

\sketch For the difference $w$ of two solutions, define

\[ e(t)=\frac12\int _U(w_t^2+|Dw|^2)\, dx. \]

The homogeneous wave equation and integration by parts give

\[ e'(t)=\int _Uw_t(w_{tt}-\Delta w)\, dx=0, \]

with no boundary term because $w=w_t=0$ on the lateral boundary. Initial data give $e(0)=0$, so $w_t=Dw=0$ and $w=0$.

□
